persons.note: AN ARRIVAL WITH A MONTH, WHICH ONLY SIX HOUSEHOLDS IN THIS PARCEL HAVE. He is also the man whose name is attached in the Chicago literature to the first balloon-frame building - St Mary's - and this record makes no claim about that, because Andreas calls him the architect and says nothing about the framing method. HE IS IN THE DATASET BECAUSE THE 1835 TOWN CANNOT BE BUILT WITHOUT HIS TRADE. Andreas's roster is the only list this project holds that names artisans at all, and every name on it is a documented alternative to an inferred one. THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 2 times, as “TAYLOR A D”, 1836-06-23 to 1836-06-28: 2 lots in the platted town — lot 2 of block 42 in the town the register codes CHIOT (L2BL42CHIOT, as printed); lot 8 of block 6 in the town the register codes CHI (L8BL6CHI, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $5430.00 (ls1482, ls1483). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $5430.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: TAYLOR A D matches Augustine Deodat Taylor: the forename names Augustine Deodat Taylor of the 7 people of this surname, and the forename agrees as an initial only. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict. FERGUS 1839'S LATER LISTS — 1837 AND 1839 EVIDENCE, NEVER AN 1835 FACT. Fergus' Chicago Directory for 1839 names this person 1 time in its two later lists: the poll of Chicago's first city election, 2 May 1837 — “Augustin D.
